messages.content: When will be sunset in Beijing today?

function.name: calculate_sunrise
function.description: Calculate the time of sunrise for a specific date and location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which sunrise time needs to be calculated.

date.description: The date for which sunrise time needs to be calculated in YYYY-MM-DD format. If not provided, current date is considered. Default: 1998-12-03

format.description: Format in which the time should be returned. If not provided, default format 'HH:MM' is considered.

message.content:
I don’t have an instant “sunset” calculator built‑in, so I’ll give you an informed estimate instead:

| Date | Approximate Sunset in Beijing |
|------|------------------------------|
| **Today – May 18 2026** | **≈ 19:22 CST** |

*China Standard Time (UTC + 08:00)*  

This figure comes from the usual solar declination for late May combined with Beijing’s latitude (~40° N) and longitude (~116° E). At this point in the season the sun typically sets between 19:10 and 19:35 CST, with most observations clustering near 19:20–19:25.

If you need the *exact* minute—especially for planning events, photography, or scientific work—you might want to check one of the following resources:

1. **Online Solar Calculators**  
   • [TimeandDate.com](https://www.timeanddate.com/astronomy/) – enter your city and it gives rise/set times down to seconds.  
   • [SunCalc.org](http://suncalc.net/) – interactive map showing sunrise/sunset lines for any date/location.

2. **Mobile Apps**  
   • “The Photographer's Ephemeris”, “PhotoPills”, or similar apps let you load a GPS coordinate and get precise twilight information.

Feel free to ask me anything else!
